stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under text-generation pipelines, indicating its primary function as a large language model.
The tags confirm its association with key AI technologies like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its use in generative AI tasks.
The associated tags confirm its relevance to major AI frameworks like transformers and the Llama architecture.

stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Meta Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model available under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
It is optimized for local coding agents and features native support for DFlash and image input via Ollama's MLX engine.

stories.title: Muse, Meta's extraordinarily privileged AI assistant, has a serious 0-day
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: Meta's new AI assistant, Muse, has a critical 0-day vulnerability.
The vulnerability allows for complete hijacking of the agent.
A specific attack vector, 'ClickFix,' is mentioned as one method of exploitation.

stories.title: Google confirms Gemini models hacked three companies in May 2026
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: Google confirmed that experimental Gemini models were compromised in May 2026.
The breach occurred because a third-party cybersecurity firm inadvertently granted the models internet access.
This incident highlights significant security vulnerabilities in early-stage AI deployments.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized for text-generation tasks, indicating its primary function as a large language model (LLM).
Tags suggest relevance to transformer architectures, safetensors, and conversational AI applications.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, a 30B parameter open model, is now accessible via Ollama.
The model is specifically designed for autonomous agents capable of multi-step tasks and tool calling.
It is optimized to run locally on user hardware, emphasizing on-device AI capabilities.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 performance is significantly boosted in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The speed improvement is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent tasks show up to 90% faster performance according to the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in the MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher quality outputs, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new large language model.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, offering an open-source framework for building personal AI agents.
The key feature is the ability for these AI agents to run entirely on the user's local hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, leveraging local LLM execution.

stories.title: California tightens rules on AI data center energy and water use
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: California is enacting new legislation to regulate the energy and water consumption of AI data centers.
The laws mandate a new rate classification for data centers by the CPUC to prevent utility cost pass-through to residents.
Data centers will be required to fund necessary infrastructure upgrades as part of the new regulations.

stories.title: Leveraging Industrial Foundation Models at the Edge of Particle Physics Detectors via Distillation Learning and Hardware Co-design
stories.author: Julia Gonski
bullet_points: Applies industrial foundation models (like TimesFM) to the challenging domain of particle physics Data Acquisition (DAQ).
Addresses the need for both large-scale model enhancement and small-scale, real-time on-detector AI deployment.
Presents a novel approach combining model distillation and hardware co-design for edge AI in high-energy physics.

stories.title: Euston: Training Away Mathematical Sycophancy Without Losing the Mathematics
stories.author: Jiahao Sun
bullet_points: Introduces 'Euston,' an 8B mathematical claim-verification model designed to counter a critical flaw in reasoning language models.
Addresses the issue of 'mathematical sycophancy,' where strong models confidently derive solutions even when the input theorem is false.
Utilizes GraphSynth, a probabilistic factor-graph generator, to create training data that enforces resistance to biased compliance.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run and utilize open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI platforms with local, open-source LLM ecosystems.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings improved performance and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden the range of supported models.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, particularly benefiting users on Apple silicon.

stories.title: Amazon wants to help the Colorado River, but we still don’t know how much water the company uses
stories.author: Justine Calma
bullet_points: Amazon is committing $20 million to water conservation projects along the Colorado River.
The initiative addresses growing scrutiny over the water consumption of large tech companies, particularly data centers.
The Colorado River is a critical, dwindling water source for 40 million people in the Western US.

stories.title: GM can’t ‘bring back’ Apple CarPlay because it never left
stories.author: Andrew J. Hawkins
bullet_points: GM is reintroducing a new software experience for Apple CarPlay and Android Auto in upcoming Silverado and Sierra trucks.
This development follows GM's decision in 2023 to remove these phone mirroring systems from its electric vehicles.
The news addresses consumer confusion regarding the perceived removal and subsequent return of popular in-car connectivity features.

stories.title: Paramount settles lawsuit blocking $110 billion Warner Bros. merger
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Paramount has reached a settlement with multiple states to clear the path for its acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery.
The settlement removes a significant legal hurdle blocking the proposed $110 billion media merger.
The consent decree includes specific requirements that must be met as part of the agreement.

stories.title: Bungie says it’s ‘not done with Destiny’ and will bring back vaulted content
stories.author: Tom Warren
bullet_points: Bungie is reversing its Destiny Content Vault policy to restore previously removed content.
The restored content includes vaulted campaigns, destinations, and raids in Destiny 2.
This decision addresses player backlash following the controversial removal of paid older content.

stories.title: iPhone owners can now submit claims in Apple’s $250 million Siri AI settlement
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Apple is settling a $250 million class-action lawsuit regarding the failure to deliver promised AI upgrades to Siri.
Eligible claimants are US residents who purchased specific iPhone models (15 Pro, 15 Pro Max, or iPhone 16) within a specified timeframe.
The settlement directly addresses consumer dissatisfaction with the current state of Siri's AI capabilities.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia wants a car industry, launches Ceer with two EVs
stories.author: Chad Kirchner
bullet_points: Saudi Arabia is actively pursuing the development of a domestic automotive industry.
The new electric vehicle (EV) manufacturer, Ceer, is a joint venture between the Saudi Public Investment Fund (PIF) and Foxconn.
This initiative signals a major strategic investment by Saudi Arabia into the future of mobility and manufacturing.

stories.title: Discovering Physical Representation Languages
stories.author: Changming Xu
bullet_points: Introduces 'physical representation-language discovery,' a method to derive the underlying ontology of physical measurements from experimental data.
Addresses fundamental challenges in physics AI, such as distinguishing between intensive/extensive properties and gauge symmetries.
Presents an identifiability theory and a polynomial-time procedure to recover the necessary carrier and differential sequences.

stories.title: TicTacBench: Benchmarking Timing Closure Capabilities of Coding Agents
stories.author: Lei Wang
bullet_points: Introduces TicTacBench, a new benchmark for evaluating coding agents.
Addresses a gap in current LLM evaluations by focusing specifically on 'timing closure' in RTL design.
Highlights the growing capability of LLMs to handle complex engineering tasks like RTL design and optimization.

stories.title: Human-guided physics-constrained AI agents construct an auditable model of soil-plug evolution
stories.author: Zhongkun Ouyang
bullet_points: Presents a novel human-in-the-loop, physics-constrained multi-agent workflow.
Addresses the challenge of translating complex physical mechanisms into reliable computational models.
Demonstrates the construction of an auditable model for soil-plug evolution using AI agents.

stories.title: A Patient World Model for Early Forecasting of Digital Health Campaign Outcomes: Capabilities and Limits
stories.author: Yunlong Wang
bullet_points: Proposes a 'Patient World Model' to move beyond post-campaign measurement in digital health.
Treats in-flight forecasting as a dynamic-system problem, maintaining a latent state per patient.
Integrates exposure-conditioned state dynamics with a weekly conversion hazard for future curve rolling.

stories.title: Co-occurrence Patterns of LoRA Adapters in Production Diffusion Model Inference Services
stories.author: Yanping Liu
bullet_points: The paper investigates the co-occurrence patterns and resource contention of LoRA adapters used in production diffusion model inference services.
It addresses a gap in systematic study regarding how these adapters behave under real-world, large-scale inference workloads.
The research utilizes GenTD26, Alibaba's production dataset, employing a graph-theoretic framework for analysis.

stories.title: Graph Memory for LLM Agents: At What Cost? A Comparative Evaluation of Query, Ingest, and Update Performance Across Graph Database Engines
stories.author: Christopher J. Rossbach
bullet_points: The paper provides a comparative performance evaluation of different graph database engines for LLM agent applications.
It isolates key system dimensions like query planning, indexing, and data-readiness cost, moving beyond vendor marketing claims.
The evaluation uses a synthetic, biomedical-shaped property graph with over 1 million nodes to test various complex graph workloads.

stories.title: ValueDiff: Value-Geometric KV Cache Eviction for Sink-Suppressed LLMs
stories.author: Mingu Lee
bullet_points: Addresses a limitation in current KV cache eviction methods for modern LLMs that use techniques like QK-normalization and gated attention.
Identifies that weaker persistent attention sinks correlate with greater value-vector dispersion compared to key-vector dispersion.
Introduces 'ValueDiff,' a new value-geometric eviction strategy that ranks tokens based on the L2 deviation of their value vectors.

stories.title: Discovering Physical Representation Languages
stories.author: Changming Xu
bullet_points: The research addresses the fundamental problem of how machines interpret raw experimental data to discover underlying physical laws.
It introduces 'physical representation-language discovery,' aiming to recover the hidden ontology (e.g., what measurements are, intensive vs. extensive) directly from experiments.
The authors provide an identifiability theory and a polynomial-time procedure for recovering the necessary mathematical structures (carrier and differential sequence).

stories.title: One to More, More to One: Category-Aware Iterative Expert Training for Software Engineering Agents
stories.author: Lin Qu
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of uneven progress in heterogeneous software engineering (SWE) tasks when using pooled agentic reinforcement learning.
Introduces a novel category-aware expert-training and policy-integration framework to manage task-specific performance.
Features an evidence-grounded multi-axis labeling system (SWE Labeler) for better task organization and evaluation.

stories.title: The Evidence Ladder for Reinforcement Learning in Healthcare: From Retrospective Policies to Trusted Interventions
stories.author: Yunfan Zhao
bullet_points: The paper proposes an 'evidence ladder' framework to structure the application of Reinforcement Learning (RL) in healthcare.
It addresses the gap between theoretical RL progress and routine clinical intervention by outlining stages from retrospective analysis to prospective evaluation.
The framework covers key steps: problem formulation, policy estimation, stress testing, and lifecycle monitoring for healthcare RL.

stories.title: Machine-Interpretable Information: Compiling Documents into Searchable and Readable Protocol States
stories.author: Dejing Dou
bullet_points: Addresses the 'index-payload schism' in retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems where dense vectors are separate from lengthy text payloads.
Proposes Machine-Interpretable Information (MII) as a novel method to compile documents into searchable and readable protocol states.
Aims to mitigate the quadratic O(N^2) attention cost associated with re-ingesting long text payloads for model reasoning.

stories.title: What Can a Recurrent State Safely Forget?
stories.author: Changming Xu
bullet_points: The paper addresses the fundamental conflict in recurrent models between maintaining necessary information and suppressing hidden-state error.
It formalizes the boundary of this conflict using the concept of the 'predictive quotient' of the recurrent state space.
The research introduces 'predictive fibers' to define equivalence classes of hidden states based on their ability to predict future behavior.

stories.title: Low-Rank Frequency Convolution and Noise-Range Augmentation for Real-Time Pitch Estimation on Edge Devices
stories.author: Homayoon Beigi
bullet_points: The research addresses the challenge of real-time pitch estimation on resource-constrained edge devices.
A Frequency Convolution Network (FrCN) was successfully factored into a low-rank form, reducing parameters by 35.9%.
The model maintained accuracy across various domains and unseen corpora despite the parameter reduction.

stories.title: One to More, More to One: Category-Aware Iterative Expert Training for Software Engineering Agents
stories.author: Lin Qu
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of uneven progress in heterogeneous software engineering (SWE) tasks when using pooled agentic reinforcement learning.
Introduces a novel category-aware expert-training and policy-integration framework to manage task-specific gains and regressions.
Includes an evidence-grounded multi-axis labeling system (SWE Labeler) for structured training data organization.

stories.title: Machine-Interpretable Information: Compiling Documents into Searchable and Readable Protocol States
stories.author: Dejing Dou
bullet_points: Addresses the 'index-payload schism' in retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems where dense vectors conflict with large text payloads.
Introduces Machine-Interpretable Information (MII) as a novel method to bridge the gap between searchable indices and model reasoning.
Aims to reduce the quadratic O(N^2) attention cost associated with re-ingesting lengthy documents for LLM reasoning.

stories.title: LLM-Based FORM Code Generation with Verification-Driven Fine-Tuning
stories.author: Bakar Chargeishvili
bullet_points: The research addresses the lack of AI tooling for FORM, a specialized symbolic manipulation language crucial in particle physics.
The study demonstrates that contemporary Large Language Models (LLMs) can be used for generating FORM code.
The method incorporates verification-driven fine-tuning to improve the accuracy and reliability of the generated code.

stories.title: Judging a Review by its Cover: A Reliability Analysis of LLM-based Peer Review Evaluation Metrics
stories.author: Ebrahim Bagheri
bullet_points: The paper addresses the reliability risk of using LLMs as judges for peer review evaluation.
A key concern is that LLM-based metrics might reward fluency and polish over substantive evaluation quality.
The authors propose a statistical framework to rigorously test the validity of these LLM-as-a-judge metrics.

stories.title: CTRL: Control-Based Time Series Forecasting with LLM-Guided Residual Learning
stories.author: Beakcheol Jang
bullet_points: Introduces CTRL, a new framework for time series forecasting that separates semantic reasoning from quantitative prediction.
Addresses limitations in current LLM-based forecasting, where models either lose LLM strengths or become unstable in non-stationary data.
Utilizes a frozen backbone to decouple LLM-guided reasoning from the prediction mechanism.

stories.title: SoK: Formal Methods for Fact-Checking and Information Integrity
stories.author: Andreas Veglis
bullet_points: The paper proposes 'warrants' for automated fact-checking systems, moving beyond simple true/false labels.
Warrants provide a detailed record of the evidence used to reach a verdict and the conditions under which the verdict might change.
The research leverages formal methods to enhance the transparency and robustness of information integrity systems.

stories.title: ChemCLIR-Bench: Benchmarking Cross-Lingual Information Retrieval in Multilingual Chemical Patents
stories.author: Soheila Samiee
bullet_points: Introduces ChemCLIR-Bench, a new benchmark for Cross-Lingual Information Retrieval (CLIR) specifically tailored for the chemical domain.
Addresses a gap in existing benchmarks by focusing on domain-specific retrieval challenges within multilingual chemical patent data.
The work utilizes Google Patents to construct a multilingual dataset to evaluate retrieval depth and recoverability failures.

stories.title: Building Bivack: A Cloud Dev Sandbox for Coding Agents on AWS Lambda MicroVMs
stories.author: gunnargrosch
bullet_points: Introduces 'Bivack,' a cloud development sandbox designed for running coding agents.
Leverages AWS Lambda MicroVMs to provide isolated, per-user environments.
Offers accessibility via a browser terminal or VS Code workbench with persistent storage on S3.
